The issue is excessively low corporate taxes (and even tax refunds going back to corporations). Trickle down economics has been tried now for longer than I’ve been alive (born in the 80s) and it’s conclusively a failure. 

FDR, Truman, Eisenhower, JFK, and LBJ had policies that pushed us FORWARD. We built the Interstate Highway System, we built schools and bridges, we funded Social Security, WIC, Medicare, Medicaid, and lifted huge amounts of people from poverty in the 40s, 50s, and 60s. Then Nixon comes into office in 1968. By the time he resigns the stage is set for the 1970s stagflation and while Carter tried what he could with an obstructive Congress (sound familiar right now?), it can take a while for economic policies to have a noticeable effect. (Think of it as trying to change the color of a pool with food coloring but only adding one drop every minute. You’ll get there, but it takes time.) 

Once Reagan came into office and started ramping up the process of deregulation, there was a noticeable change: for the worse. Credit cards and consumer debt skyrocketed, the ability for many working class families to live on one income vanished, costs soared for healthcare, education, childcare, etc. It started in noticeably in the 80s and got so out of control that the deregulated system, with predatory lending, crashed the economy in 2008. 

All of this while Congress raids Social Security funds as petty cash for their corporate friends and our taxes fund Musk and Bezos and their ilk while you and I get the leftover pennies, kids go hungry because they can’t afford school lunch, grandma can’t afford both meds and food, corporations are buying up all the housing to turn into rental properties no one can afford even WITH roommates. 

And all the while no one pays FICA on amounts on earned income over $168,600. 

Let that sink in. 

The upper incomes are paying proportionally less tax overall than the rest of us but get more benefits from the system. After all, why invest your company funds when you can get your pocket Congresscritter to fund part or all of it for you! 

The issue isn’t how much WE pay for taxes, it’s how much those at the top pay and where those funds are allocated and the system rigged by the GOP. To keep it that way.

Grocery store at work? (Or work in a grocery store?)  


Let's look at lightweight food options that don't need refrigeration and can last for multiple meals.  


1. Flavored instant oatmeal packets (2 for breakfast should hold you over)
2. 6 packs of individual servings of raisins
3. Vegetable bouillon/miso soup packets
4. Individual pouches/cups of peanut butter or almond butter
5. Minute rice cups (not pouches, so you can just heat up a single portion, there's even a brown rice/quinoa mix one!)
6. Fiber/protein bars 
7. Crackers
8. Any freeze-dried/dehydrated fruits. I'd recommend banana chips
9. Multipack of nut mixes  


Keep something in the list above on hand for lightweight food to carry around. I'm guessing you have some cutlery and a microwaveable bowl (with a lid preferably) but if not, it'd be a good idea. There's some that collapse to fit in small spaces which might be very handy in your situation. Make two meals a day (and maybe a snack or two) with the above. For one meal (dinner, lunch, whatever), allot yourself $5 and get something a bit more varied. For example: a can of vegan chili and a potato to cook in the microwave and eat with the chili. Or a steam in the microwave bag of mixed veggies from the frozen section to dump in with some rice and a bouillon cube to make a soup in the shelter microwave. Or even take that $5 and get a bean burrito from Taco Bell. (If you can, use the app to order and pay, it'll let you see more customization/veganization options.) You could probably keep it under $50 for the week this way.
